Subject: Request: tri-region architects deep dive (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Hannah + Ben,

Thanks for the quick responses on the intake form. We’re trying to line up a technical deep-dive with our architects: Mats (Sweden), Asha (APAC), and our US platform team. Ideally we’d like one 90-minute session, but our folks suggested splitting into 45-minute focused blocks may be easier to coordinate given timezones and local working hours.

Constraints:
- Mats can’t start before 09:30 CET on weekdays.
- Asha is in IST and prefers sessions after 10:30 IST.
- Our US team needs something not earlier than 08:30 PT.

We’re aware DST is in play this quarter (US changes earlier than EU) — that’s one reason we wanted your guidance so invites don’t drift in the weeks after the meeting.

Attached: desired_agenda.docx (high level topics).

Can your team propose a schedule (single 90min vs split) and any recurring pattern that makes this repeatable if we do a series?

Best,
Samantha
Head of Integrations, FintechCo

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: tri-region architects deep dive (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks — this is totally doable. Quick suggestion before we pick times: rather than one long 90-minute block we often run a rolling "engineer block" pattern that gives focused 30–45 minute windows for architecture, then a short break and a follow-up block that a different engineer attends. Benefits: easier to land across three zones, less context fatigue for SEs, and easier to rotate people across weeks without moving the anchor.

High-level proposal (I attached an availability_grid.xlsx with people slots):
- Option A: Single 90-min UTC-anchored session (less scheduling overhead but harder for APAC).
- Option B (preferred): Rolling 3-hour anchor window broken into three 45-min blocks; we schedule the block most convenient for the customer each week and rotate which Redwood engineer covers which block.

We’ll include clear UTC times on the invites and mark the invites as UTC-anchored so calendar clients don’t shift when DST transitions occur. See attached availability_grid.xlsx.

If you’re OK with Option B I can send a concrete 2-week sample with exact local conversions.

—Hannah
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 15:20:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: rolling blocks & UTC-anchored invites for tri-region deep dive

Folks — quick technical notes to include in the sample: DST mismatch windows are the tricky bit. Two practical guardrails I recommend we surface in the invite and in the Ops note: 

1) Always display the meeting as "Anchored to UTC" in the title and put local conversions in the body (e.g., 13:00–13:45 UTC = 06:00 PT / 14:00 CET / 19:30 IST) so attendees see where the anchor is.
2) For recurring series that overlap a DST boundary we: a) create calendar instances only 2–4 weeks out and b) send a quick "DST check" email 7 days prior when either US/EU transition is within the next 2 weeks.

Concrete options for next week (all options are 45-min blocks inside a 3-hour anchor):
- Option 1: 13:00–13:45 UTC (06:00 PT / 14:00 CET / 19:30 IST) — early for US, borderline for APAC.
- Option 2: 15:00–15:45 UTC (08:00 PT / 16:00 CET / 21:30 IST) — tries to hit later APAC, earlier US morning.
- Option 3: 17:00–17:45 UTC (10:00 PT / 18:00 CET / 23:15 IST) — late for APAC but sometimes acceptable if they prefer evenings.

I recommend Option 2 as the default weekly slot; fallback Option 1 if APAC cannot attend.

I’ve also dropped a timezone_conversions.png into the shared drive for quick visual reference.

—Vivek
Director, Solutions Reliability
